en: Ganthaganthaniyaduka (The Dyad of the Bound and the Binder)
Dependent on a state that is both unbound and not conducive to bondage, there arises a state that is both unbound and not conducive to bondage by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is both unbound and not conducive to bondage, there arises a state that is not conducive to bondage and is neither bound nor conducive to bondage by way of the root-condition. Dependent on a state that is both unbound and not conducive to bondage...
Dependent on a state that is both not a tie and not conducive to ties, there arise states that are neither conducive to ties nor a tie,
Dependent on a state that is both not conducive to ties and not a tie, there arises a state that is not conducive to ties and not a tie.
And a state that is neither a bond nor conducive to bondage arises with a root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither a bond nor conducive to bondage, a state that is neither a bond nor conducive to bondage arises with a root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither a bond nor conducive to bondage, a state that is neither a bond nor conducive to bondage... [and so forth].

Dependent on states that are both not-fetters and not-fettering, and neither-fetter nor fetter, there arise states that are both not-fetters and not-fettering by way of root-condition. … [three] … (Abbreviated.
Nine in the case of roots … pe … one in the case of resultants … pe … nine in the case of non-disappearance. (Full detail for all.)
